saml.description: The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens; requesting offline_access is ignored.
saml.note: Do not treat missing refresh_token in the token response after SAML authentication as a bug.

saml.description: Dex uses the SAML NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and never changes.
saml.note: Differences in emailAttr or usernameAttr alone do not imply a different downstream principal if NameID is unchanged.

saml.description: Dex requires sending the initial AuthnRequest and validates the SAML Response InResponseTo value rather than accepting unprompted AuthnResponses.
saml.note: A rejected unsolicited SAMLResponse is expected behavior, not evidence of a broken login flow.

saml.description: Dex documentation warns the SAML connector is unmaintained and likely vulnerable, and may be deprecated.
saml.note: This is a documentation warning, not a specific oracle condition; use it to prioritize findings but not as a test result by itself.

saml.constraint: Dex's documented dynamic management API is gRPC only; the documentation does not provide REST/JSON admin endpoints for creating connectors, clients, users, policies, or auth methods. Do NOT assume REST setup operations such as enable_auth_method, create_provider, create_application, create_user, or cleanup_auth_method exist from these docs.

For SAML login tests, the fuzzer MUST run an SP-initiated flow first and preserve the returned state/relay context, because Dex sends the initial AuthnRequest and validates the SAML Response InResponseTo value. Unprompted or IdP-initiated SAMLResponses will be rejected by design and are not evidence of stronger validation.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution, create the SAML connector with insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true if you want to test the insecure configuration path. The default documented configuration uses ca/caData for signature validation; without explicitly disabling validation, attacker-signed assertions should be rejected.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch, configure the SAML connector with ssoIssuer set. If ssoIssuer is omitted, Dex has no documented expected Issuer value to compare against, so an issuer-mismatch test may pass trivially because issuer validation was never configured.

For I5 saml_wrong_audience and saml_no_audience_restriction, configure entityIssuer when possible. If entityIssuer is unset, Dex uses redirectURI as the expected audience for AudienceRestriction evaluation; tests must compare against that exact value, not an inferred SP entity ID.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, include a control SAML login with a valid assertion before the expired assertion attempt. Otherwise a failed expired-assertion login cannot be distinguished from generic connector misconfiguration such as wrong CA, wrong callback URL, or InResponseTo mismatch.

For I2 replay tests against SAML, Dex documentation states it persists state to prevent replays. The fuzzer MUST reuse the same assertion identifier and same assertion material when testing replay; merely performing two separate successful SAML logins is not a replay test because each fresh assertion is expected to succeed.

For I4 identity-collision tests on the SAML connector, Dex binds the downstream user identity to the SAML NameID value, which it assumes is unique and immutable. The fuzzer MUST vary NameID itself for principal-binding tests; changing only usernameAttr or emailAttr values does not change the primary identity key.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision, a mismatch between NameID and email should NOT be treated as a collision unless the granted downstream subject follows the victim email rather than the attacker NameID. Dex documentation says NameID is the unique identifier, while emailAttr and usernameAttr are only mapped claims.

For I5 group-based authorization tests, allowedGroups is list-membership against exact group values from the SAML assertion. There is no documented companion match-mode parameter. Wildcards such as '*' are literal strings, not patterns. For multi-identity scenarios requiring different groups to pass the same connector, OMIT allowedGroups rather than setting a wildcard.

For I5 group filtering tests, distinguish authentication gating from claim filtering: allowedGroups controls whether authentication succeeds based on membership in at least one configured group, while filterGroups=true only removes non-allowed groups from the emitted groups claim. Do not interpret dropped extra groups as an authorization failure.

For I2 offline_access and refresh-token expectations on SAML, Dex documentation states the SAML connector ignores offline_access and does not support refresh tokens. Do NOT flag absence of refresh_token after SAML login as a freshness bug.

For I1/I5 OIDC token handling after SAML upstream login, remember Dex is the OIDC provider to the client. The credential used for subsequent API calls is access_token from /token, not id_token. Any verification logic that treats id_token as the bearer session token will mis-test the platform.

For password-grant setup, the password grant only works when oauth2.passwordConnector is configured and the password grant type is enabled. A 4xx from /token with grant_type=password is not a user-authentication failure unless those prerequisites are present.

Token exchange is only documented for OIDC upstream connectors, not SAML connectors. Do NOT attempt to use token_exchange as a SAML upstream test primitive; any such failure is by design and not an authorization-binding issue in the SAML connector.

Dex's documented dynamic management API is gRPC only; the documentation does not provide REST admin endpoints for connector/client CRUD. The fuzzer MUST use gRPC for create_provider/enable_auth_method/create_application and MUST NOT assume equivalent HTTP admin paths exist.

For SAML login tests, Dex only accepts SP-initiated flows and validates InResponseTo. The sequence MUST call start_oidc_auth first and preserve the returned state/flow context before posting saml_login. Sending an unsolicited SAMLResponse directly to the callback will be rejected by design and is not an I3 finding.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution insecure-default testing, create the SAML connector with insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true or without CA-based validation only when intentionally testing insecure configuration. If signature validation is configured with ca/caData, attacker-signed assertions should be rejected; acceptance under insecureSkipSignatureValidation is by configuration, not a bug.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure ssoIssuer on the SAML connector. If ssoIssuer is omitted, issuer comparison may be skipped because the expected issuer is not pinned; a passing forged-issuer login in that setup is inconclusive and must not be treated as a validation bypass.

For I5 saml_wrong_audience and saml_no_audience_restriction tests, configure entityIssuer when you need a specific expected audience. If entityIssuer is unset, Dex uses redirectURI as the expected audience for AudienceRestriction evaluation. The oracle MUST compare against the actual configured expected audience source, not assume a separate SP entity ID.

For I1/I5 destination and audience tests, the SAML assertion/response Destination must exactly match redirectURI when a Destination element is present. A mismatch causes rejection by design and should not be confused with signature or issuer enforcement.

Dex uses NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and immutable. For I4 multi-identity tests, vary NameID to test principal binding. Changing only email/username attributes while keeping the same NameID is expected to map to the same principal and is not a collision bug.

nameIDPolicyFormat is not a wildcard or pattern-matching field; it selects a concrete SAML NameID format value, defaulting to persistent. For I4 tests requiring multiple upstream identities to authenticate through one connector, do NOT treat this field as a matcher and do NOT use wildcard values.

allowedGroups performs list-membership filtering against SAML group attribute values, not glob or regex matching. For multi-identity scenarios, every tested identity must actually carry at least one allowed group, or the fuzzer must omit allowedGroups entirely. Setting allowedGroups to '*' will only match a literal '*' group if present.

If filterGroups=true, Dex removes all groups not present in allowedGroups from the resulting claims. I5 group-based authorization tests MUST account for this post-filtering behavior; missing groups in downstream tokens may be by design rather than evidence of claim loss or confusion.

The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens and ignores offline_access. Tests that expect a refresh_token after SAML authentication MUST NOT treat its absence as a bug; use authorization_code exchange and access/id token inspection only.

For I2 SAML freshness tests such as saml_expired_assertion, include a control flow with a valid assertion first. A failed expired assertion without a successful control cannot distinguish proper expiry enforcement from broken connector/client setup.

Dex's OAuth2 password grant only works when oauth2.passwordConnector is configured and the password grant is enabled. For SAML profiles, login_with_password is for admin/setup access to Dex itself, not for exercising the SAML connector. A password-grant failure without passwordConnector configured is by design.

Token exchange is documented as supported only with OIDC connectors, not SAML connectors. The fuzzer MUST NOT attempt to use token_exchange as a SAML upstream test primitive; use the SAML browser flow followed by code exchange instead.

Numeric sentinel semantics are not documented for SAML connector fields in the provided docs. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0, empty string, or omitted values disable validation or mean literal zero for any undocumented duration/limit field; only documented defaults such as nameIDPolicyFormat=persistent should be relied upon.

Dex SAML connector is configured statically in the config file; the provided docs do not describe an HTTP admin API for creating or modifying SAML connectors. The fuzzer MUST treat create_provider/enable_auth_method as out-of-band config provisioning, not runtime REST calls.

Dex API is gRPC-only for dynamic management. The docs explicitly state v2 API is entirely gRPC and not REST. Any setup operation using Dex API (such as create_application) MUST use the gRPC service, not guessed HTTP endpoints.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution, Dex SAML connector supports skipping signature validation via config.insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true. To test secure behavior, the fuzzer MUST configure a CA (ca or caData) and MUST NOT enable insecureSkipSignatureValidation. If insecureSkipSignatureValidation is true, acceptance of attacker-signed assertions is by design and not a vulnerability.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch, configure config.ssoIssuer to the expected IdP issuer. The docs mark ssoIssuer as optional; if omitted, issuer comparison may not be enforced. The fuzzer MUST include a control with correct issuer and an attack with idp_entity_id set to an untrusted issuer to distinguish missing configuration from a validation bypass.

For I5 saml_wrong_audience and saml_no_audience_restriction, audience validation depends on Dex redirectURI unless entityIssuer is configured, in which case entityIssuer overrides redirectURI as the required audience. The fuzzer MUST compute expected AudienceRestriction against entityIssuer when present, otherwise against redirectURI; otherwise results will be misinterpreted.

For I3 flow-coherence tests on SAML responses, Dex requires SP-initiated flow and validates InResponseTo. The sequence MUST begin with start_oidc_auth and saml_login MUST be sent with metadata.initiate_saml_flow=true so the fabricated SAMLResponse matches the issued AuthnRequest. Sending unsolicited/unprompted responses is rejected by design and is not an I3 failure.

For I4 multi-identity tests, Dex SAML connector binds the upstream identity to the SAML NameID value. The docs state NameID is used as the user's unique identifier and should be unique and immutable. Therefore tests for cross-user collision MUST vary NameID itself; changing only email or username attributes while keeping NameID constant is expected to map to the same principal.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision, use different NameID and email values because Dex uses NameID as unique identifier, while emailAttr only maps a claim. If two logins with different NameID but same email do not merge, that is expected behavior; do not treat lack of email-based linking as a bug.

For I5 group-based authorization tests, allowedGroups is list-membership exact matching against SAML group values, not wildcard or regex matching. No companion match-type parameter is documented. For multi-identity scenarios requiring different groups to pass the same connector, the fuzzer MUST OMIT allowedGroups rather than set wildcard-like values such as '*', which would be treated as a literal group name.

For I5 group filtering tests, filterGroups=true does not deny authentication by itself; it excludes groups not in allowedGroups from emitted claims. Authentication gating is based on membership in configured allowedGroups when groupsAttr is set. The fuzzer MUST distinguish claim filtering from login denial when evaluating authorization outcomes.

For I2 freshness tests on SAML assertions (expired_assertion, replay, OneTimeUse), include a CONTROL login with a valid assertion in the same connector/client setup before the mutated assertion. Without a control, a failed login may reflect broken SAML setup rather than freshness enforcement.

Dex SAML connector does not support refresh tokens and ignores offline_access for SAML logins. Tests that expect refresh_token issuance, refresh-based replay, or offline session semantics after SAML authentication MUST NOT treat absence of refresh_token as a bug.

OAuth2 grantTypes has a documented default when omitted: if grantTypes is not specified, Dex enables authorization_code, refresh_token, and urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange. Omitted/unspecified does NOT mean no grants. The fuzzer MUST explicitly set grantTypes when testing grant enable/disable behavior to avoid relying on permissive defaults.

SAML nameIDPolicyFormat has a documented default sentinel-by-omission: if unspecified, it defaults to urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent. The fuzzer MUST not assume omission leaves NameID format unconstrained; omission selects persistent format.

For I1 signature-integrity variants such as saml_unsigned_assertion or saml_spurious_signature, the docs only state Dex validates the response signature using the configured CA and do not document support for signed AuthnRequests or encrypted attributes. The fuzzer SHOULD test whether Dex accepts envelope-only signatures versus assertion signatures, but MUST interpret failures carefully because the documentation does not specify assertion-level signature requirements.

For token_exchange I5 tests, Dex documentation states token exchange currently works only with OIDC connectors, not SAML connectors. The fuzzer MUST NOT expect RFC 8693 token exchange to operate directly on SAML upstream connectors; any such setup failure is by design.

For OIDC authorization requests used to reach the SAML connector, scope MUST include openid. Dex documentation states openid is required for all login requests. Missing openid causing failure is expected and not evidence of stricter-than-documented behavior.
